cases.text: A tracked change modifies `command.go` around how a subcommand's `GroupID` is checked against its parent's registered help groups. Retrieve the validation function, the call site that runs it before a command executes, and the tests confirming a missing group panics both at the root level and for a nested child command. Keep the impact set to the group-validation panic path, not general help-group text rendering.
cases.rationale: `checkCommandGroups` is invoked from `ExecuteC` before dispatch and panics on an unregistered `GroupID`; the impact set should stay on the validation/panic path and its two precedence tests, not the separate group-label rendering in help/usage output or the unrelated flag-group feature.

cases.text: When a Cobra CLI user mistypes a subcommand, the program sometimes prints 'Did you mean this?' with a nearby command name. I want to see the matching algorithm behind that — is it Levenshtein distance, a prefix check, or an explicit alias list — and confirm this typo-correction path is separate from shell tab-completion. Point me to the matching function and its test.
cases.rationale: The word 'completion' in the prompt invites retrieving the shell tab-completion engine; the actual typo-suggestion logic is `Command.SuggestionsFor`/`findSuggestions` in command.go, unrelated to completions.go's shell scripts, so the negative selector checks the retriever isn't misled by the naming overlap.

cases.text: I've built a CLI with Cobra and want to publish it as a Homebrew formula so macOS users can `brew install` it directly. Where in this repository is the Homebrew tap or formula generation handled?
cases.rationale: Cobra generates shell completion scripts and command docs but has no code for building or publishing distribution packages like Homebrew formulas; that is an external packaging concern (e.g. goreleaser) with no implementation anywhere in this repository. The only 'Homebrew' hit is an unrelated comment about the bash-completion version shipped on Homebrew systems, not formula generation, so a correct system abstains instead of citing it.
